topTools.name: previewTool
topTools.description: Interact with the Preview view. Use this tool to send a sequence of commands (DSL) to interact with the running preview. This is for TESTING and SIMULATING USER INTERACTION, not for editing the project. For editing the project, use sceneOps, setupGameScript, or compileProject instead. Available commands: screenshot, touch, touch_down, touch_up, touch_move, drag, wait, reset_preview, start_preview_record, stop_preview_record, record_preview_video_mp4, pause_preview, resume_preview, transport_preview_property.

intention.description: What you are trying to achieve with this interaction.

topTools.name: consoleLog
topTools.description: Retrieve runtime console logs from the Effect House project. Use this tool to get script logs, debug information, and runtime output from the currently running preview or compiled project.

startLine.description: 1-based log line to start reading from. If omitted, reads the latest logs.

count.description: Number of logs to retrieve. Default is 200.

topTools.name: playLifecycle
topTools.description: Control Game eval playthrough lifecycle. Use "start" to reset Preview, start runtime logging and round video recording, wait 400ms for the current run log, and pause. Use "restart" after a terminal state to record it for 3 seconds, restart gameplay, and keep writing the same round video. Use "finish" to record the terminal state for 3 seconds, stop runtime logging, save the round video, resume Preview, and reset it.

action.description: Use "start" to begin recording, "restart" to restart gameplay in the same recording, or "finish" to save it.

topTools.name: playScreenshot
topTools.description: Capture a Preview screenshot for the current Game eval playthrough. It uses the fixed Preview scale 0.5 to reduce image token cost; call it with no arguments.

topTools.name: playStep
topTools.description: Advance the current Game eval playthrough by one controlled step. It executes Preview actions, looping switch_human_action entries, and simulated audio detector inputs in the supplied order, waits waitAfterMs after each action, then pauses Preview again. Audio inputs are serialized with touch and human actions; pitch, volume, and one keyword event may be combined in one audio action. Before the first volume action, read the game input mapping and use a small calibration value; raw detector volume is not normalized gameplay strength. Use multiple actions in one call for a coherent operation such as tap sequences, press-move-release, or short interaction chains. Choose reasonable non-zero waits so the runtime can process each command before the next one. Coordinates are normalized Preview coordinates in [0, 1].

params.description: Params for the Preview action command.

waitAfterMs.description: Runtime duration to wait after this action before the next action or final pause, in milliseconds.

actionId.description: Exact action id returned by playHumanActions.

waitAfterMs.description: Runtime duration to wait after this action before the next action or final pause, in milliseconds.

pitchHz.description: Simulated pitch detector output in Hz.

volume.description: Raw volume detector output in [0, 1], not normalized gameplay strength. Read the game mapping before first use and start with a small calibration value because values such as 0.1 may already saturate.

keywords.description: Keywords reported by the simulated detector hit.

waitAfterMs.description: Runtime duration to wait after this action before the next action or final pause, in milliseconds.

actions.description: Ordered Preview, human, and simulated audio actions to execute in one controlled step.

topTools.name: playState
topTools.description: Query exact Game runtime field paths for the current eval playthrough. Use playStateFields first when field names are unknown. Range can be the last N runtime frames or the runtime frames after the previous pause boundary.

fieldNames.description: Exact runtime field paths, for example ["score"], ["game.started"], ["activeScene.猪猪存钱罐.transform.screenPosition"], or ["extra.dt"].

frameCount.description: Number of latest runtime messages to inspect.

topTools.name: playStateFields
topTools.description: Return a flat fieldNames array of directly queryable root, game, and activeScene paths without their values. The array can be passed directly to playState target.fieldNames.

topTools.name: playHumanActions
topTools.description: List the human actions available to the current Game eval playthrough. Each action includes an exact id, its face/hand/fullbody category, and a recommended wait before the looping video repeats.

topTools.name: sceneOps
topTools.description: Manage the Initial State and Layout of the scene (Editor View). Use this tool to set or modify STATIC properties like default text content, starting positions, colors, and textures. PREFERRED over modifying scripts directly for static changes. To add built-in components like GameRankingList or CheckinRankingList, use type "General" with general.kind and general.properties. For a Loki GAN preset, first use ganEffect with operation:"list", then add it with type:"General", id set to the returned name, and general.kind set to the returned ganKey. Provide an array in the ops field. Each object item: {op:"add|modify|remove", id:string, ...fields}. To hide/show a whole scene group, use {op:"modify", target:"group", groupId:string, visible:false/true}. Prefer group visibility for same-phase UI sets instead of toggling each child. To hide/show an existing object, use op:"modify" with visible:false/true; type can be omitted for visible-only changes. For one phase UI set, keep one visibility control unit: either the parent group or its child objects, not both. Use op:"remove" for explicit delete/remove requests. For mention-provided runtime-only objects, pass guid on modify ops so runtime can resolve them when they are not in displayList. Positioning uses an explicit positionMode field. Use absolute for direct center-point placement with x and y, pinned for edge-based placement with left/right/top/bottom, and relative for nudging an existing object with dx and dy. For Image and Text, x/y are the center of the final width/height rectangle, never its left/top edge. Image uses textureKey, optional drawMode (Normal|Tiled|Filled|Ellipse), and optional alpha in [0,1] for opacity. Audio uses clip. PostProcess uses effectType and optional materialGuid.

x.description: Center x coordinate of the final Image/Text rectangle in the 720x1280 canvas. Never pass the left edge.

y.description: Center y coordinate of the final Image/Text rectangle in the 720x1280 canvas. Never pass the top edge.

width.description: Final display width used with the center-point x coordinate.

height.description: Final display height used with the center-point y coordinate.

alpha.description: Initial Image opacity in [0..1]. Also supported by modify Image ops.

ops.description: Array of scene operations. Choose ONE positionMode per op: absolute, pinned, or relative.

topTools.name: awaitAudioGeneration

Call this AFTER scene assembly and scripting, right before final compileProject, so the compiled project uses the real rendered audio instead of silent placeholders. Returns the list of any clip keys that ultimately failed; audio failures do not block compile.

Returns per-batch completed/failed counts and the list of any 视觉资产 key values that ultimately failed.

reason.description: Optional note describing why you are waiting now.

topTools.name: materialAsset
topTools.description: DYEH adapter for material-authoring/SKILL.md. Use create only when a new hand-written OMTL/AUSL material is required. Use edit with the existing material guid for every source change or compile-error repair; edit always rewrites in place. use read to inspect an existing .omtl, and use get_compile_status when the skill says GetMaterialCompileStatus. Do not create Materials folders, write .omtl files manually, or call a raw import path; create and edit own the asset lifecycle. Never write metadata-only OMTL or built-in Unlit shells; create and edit require Pass.Ausl plus real AUSL shader code. The create and edit responses include compileStatus mapped from ResItemMaterialOmtl.isError/errorMessage. New materials are created from a built-in Unlit material and then overwritten with omtlContent; if compileStatus.result.isError is true, fix compileStatus.result.errorMessage and retry with edit using that asset guid.

assetName.description: Material asset file name. The .omtl suffix is optional.

omtlContent.description: Full OMTL file content to write. Must include JSON header with Shader and Pass, ---ENDJSON, ---BEGIN UIPROPERTY/---END UIPROPERTY, and a non-empty inline AUSL block matching Pass.Ausl with void vertex() and void fragment(). Pass.Ausl is required; placeholder blocks like ---BEGIN undefined are invalid.

guid.description: Existing material GUID to rewrite in place.

omtlContent.description: Full OMTL file content to write. Must include JSON header with Shader and Pass, ---ENDJSON, ---BEGIN UIPROPERTY/---END UIPROPERTY, and a non-empty inline AUSL block matching Pass.Ausl with void vertex() and void fragment(). Pass.Ausl is required; placeholder blocks like ---BEGIN undefined are invalid.

guid.description: Material asset GUID to read.

assetPath.description: Material asset path to read when guid is unavailable.

Use this only when the source regions or grid are explicitly known, instead of wrapping a raster image in SVG. Do not use it for Seedream AssetBoard generation or extraction; that remains internal to seedreamEffectWorkflowBatch. The tool does not trim, resize, compress, pad, or infer crop geometry.

topTools.name: task_done

After the final write_todos completes all todos, call this tool in the same model turn if no further work remains. Note: This tool will fail if there are still pending or in-progress tasks in your todo list.

summary.description: A summary of the completed task and the results.

topTools.name: code_search
topTools.description: Code Knowledge Graph (CKG) Engine. The MOST EFFICIENT tool for exploring codebases. Use this tool when you need to understand code structure/relationships. Abilities: 1. Project Structure: List all classes/methods in the project (set mode="structure", omit file_path). 2. File Analysis: Get detailed API outline of a specific file (set mode="structure", provide file_path). 3. Symbol Navigation: Find where a symbol (class/function/variable/property) is defined (mode="definition") or used (mode="references").

file_path.description: Target file to analyze. If the user mentions a file (e.g. "in Game2D.ts"), you MUST extract it here. If omitted, structure/definition performs a project-wide scan. Set relative_path=true when file_path is relative to the current project root. For references, omitting this triggers a global search (can be slow).

relative_path.description: Whether file_path should be treated as relative to the current project root.

symbol.description: The symbol name to search for (REQUIRED for definition/references mode). E.g. class name, function name, variable name, or property name.

It waits for all three Design Brief files, then sends only Assets/design_brief_ui.md, LockedStyle, the fixed layout reference, and Style RAG-selected user style images to the setting-prompt model. It asks the setting-prompt model for the final prompt, then asks the configured setting-image model to render the setting image. It writes .agent/setting-image/设定图.png and .agent/setting-image/setting_reference.md. Seedream and scene layout read the generated artifacts automatically.

topTools.name: compileProject
topTools.description: Run the current project TypeScript verification with default settings. Call it after the editing tool has returned when you need to verify the latest persisted code; never run it in parallel with a dependent Edit, Write, or setupGameScript call. It waits for pending generated asset jobs, returns TypeScript diagnostics, and ensures a detected game entry is attached without modifying source files.
